title: Optional "smart" time-based charging to 100% when charge limit feature is in use
line: With a charge limit set, you can pick a time in the power settings and a laptop left plugged in overnight is fully charged by then.
explanation: A charge limit kept the battery at e.g. 80% forever: someone who leaves the laptop plugged in overnight and takes it out in the morning had to raise the limit by hand (with a password) and remember to lower it again, while macOS and Android top the battery up just before you usually unplug. Powerdevil had no notion of a time to be full by. The charge limit settings now have a "Charge fully by:" time (Never by default, half-hour steps), saved root-side like the limit itself. Two hours before that time, if the laptop is plugged in, powerdevil lifts the limit through a passwordless helper action that only works when an admin has set the time, and puts the limit back when the cord is unplugged (the restore from bug 445965); it skips the top-up when the cord hasn't been unplugged since the last one, so an always-docked laptop isn't held at 100%.

commits.message:
kcm: add a time of day to charge the battery fully by

With a charge limit, a laptop left plugged in overnight never had a full
battery in the morning. The charge limit settings can now set a time to
charge fully by, and powerdevil lifts the limit two hours before it.

BUG: 443761

media.caption: Master: the charge limit settings only have the stop and start levels
New "Charge fully by:" time in the charge limit settings
Plugged in at 80% with 1:30 AM set: at 11:30 PM, two hours before, the limit is lifted by itself and the applet says the battery will charge fully until unplugged
